title: Paper Town
description: Follow one man's wages backwards and see how far out of the valley they go before anyone's name is on them.

whose_wages.title: Who pays the chainman
whose_wages.objective: Ask Alder Pyke on Granary Row who pays him.
whose_wages.journal: Pyke draws one and threepence a day at the Rivermark counting house. The counting house isn't paying him; it's honouring a note for somebody else.

the_note.title: The note of hand
the_note.objective: Pyke draws his wages at the counting house. Search the Counting House for the note, read it, then bring it back to him.
the_note.journal: The counting house keeps honoured notes for a year before burning them. Pyke's note is in the tray with the rest. One bears a mark instead of a name.

followed_it.title: A name, and a river
followed_it.journal: The note is drawn on a house downriver in Greyhythe, signed by its factor, Ludo Corse. I've asked eleven people in Rivermark if they've heard of him. None has. Six are working for him, one way or another.

let_it_lie.title: Somebody's money
let_it_lie.journal: Somebody downriver is paying a chainman one and threepence a day to walk lines in a valley they don't live in. It's no crime and no business of mine. I've put the tray back where I found it.
